brief.subject: Diesel drops 19 cents, DOL contractor rule lands, theft cases
brief.headline: Diesel Falls to $5.937 as DOL Finalizes Contractor Rule and Cargo Theft Cases Mount
brief.dek: Diesel slides again, the DOL keeps its contractor rule mostly unchanged, and two big cargo theft cases hit Southern California.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 19.0 cents to $5.937 a gallon, giving owner-operators more relief at the pump heading into Thanksgiving week.

sections.heading: Diesel Keeps Sliding
bullets: $5.937 per gallon is the U.S. average retail diesel price for the week of 2026-11-16.
Down 19.0 cents (3.1%) from the prior week, a meaningful cut to per-mile fuel costs.
Down 33.9 cents over four weeks, so fuel surcharge tables may now lag what you actually pay.

sections.heading: DOL Contractor Rule Stays Put
bullets: The Labor Department's final independent contractor rule barely changed from its February proposal.
Trucking groups welcomed the rule, which replaces the Biden-era version on how contractors are classified.
Lease-on owner-operators and carriers using them should review agreements against the final text.

sections.heading: Cargo Theft Cases Pile Up
bullets: 30 months in federal prison for a trucker tied to a $7.2 million Southern California cargo theft conspiracy.
Thieves used real freight assignments and trucking companies as cover, so vet partners and loads carefully.
14 people charged in a separate $22.5 million ring that stopped moving freight trains to steal goods.
Stolen Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools and electronics were moved through storage sites into resale markets.

sections.heading: Holiday Capacity Could Tighten
bullets: Tender rejection rates could top 14% ahead of Thanksgiving, according to FreightWaves SONAR data.
Low retail inventories may drive last-minute shipping, which can lift spot opportunities for available trucks.
Possible port strikes could further squeeze capacity in some markets.

sections.heading: Rail Gains and Merger Fight
bullets: 7.3% year-over-year rise in U.S. rail traffic, with intermodal up 10.7%, adds competition for long-haul freight.
Grain carloads declined in the same week.
Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern are fighting a request to end review of their coast-to-coast merger, drawing labor support and shipper concerns.
